en: Saññojanasaññojaniyaduka (The Dyad of Fettering and the Fetterable)
Dependent on a state that is neither a fetter nor bound by a fetter, there arises a state that is neither a fetter nor bound by a fetter, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither a fetter nor bound by a fetter, there arises a state that is bound by a fetter but not a fetter, by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is neither a fetter...
Dependent on a state that is neither a fetter nor a cause for fettering,
there arise states that are both neither a fetter nor a cause for fettering and are neither a fetter nor a cause for fettering, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is both neither a fetter nor a cause for fettering and is neither a fetter, there arises a state that is both neither a fetter nor a cause for fettering and is neither a fetter, by way of root condition … three.

Dependent on a state that is neither a fetter nor an object of fettering, and which is neither an object of fettering nor not a fetter, there arises a state that is neither a fetter nor an object of fettering by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … three. (Abbreviated.
There are nine under root; nine under object … pe … one under result (*vipāka*) … pe … nine under non-disappearance (*avigata*). (Full detail for all.)
